scope: Explicit host scheduling and separation of control/worker responsibilities
status: Implemented; 36 host and 12 four-node CTest entries pass; ESP32 cross-build passes.

decisions.task_topology: User confirmed keeping the existing control task and WAMR workers.
decisions.skill: User-approved codebase-design guidance; requested refactor skill unavailable.
decisions.control: The host schedules paired lifecycle passes at explicit pre-input, post-input and staging-release checkpoints. Input and its consequences share the registry lock; output follows.
decisions.worker: Entry guard only reads current time and startup authorization while retaining the registry lock through the WAMR execution marker. Workers no longer advance graph lifecycles or consume unrelated mailboxes.
decisions.ordering: Apply node cleanup first, then two bounded edge/node rounds. Node expiry beats longer channel setup allowances; edge removals beat node startup evidence; local READY/COMMIT/ACTIVE/DISPATCH can progress without another packet.
decisions.existing_interfaces: Edge effects/owner-evidence interfaces retain their deadline guards and synchronous cleanup replies remain in control. These run on the control task.
decisions.readability: Named helpers cover platform/enrollment validation, artifact eligibility/staging selection/handoff, packet classification, output, diagnostics, deadline selection, local-role liveness and shared startup authorization.
decisions.modules: Existing host and node modules extended; no production module or concurrent task added.

baseline.note: Earlier host refactor and other uncommitted work preserved. Scope is compared with this turn snapshot.

host.exception: WAMR tests disable ASan fake stacks because the engine checks native stack addresses.
